title: Tomato and Onion Curry
subtitle: A simple vegan base curry of slow-cooked onion and tomato
excerpt: Onions cooked down until sweet and golden, then simmered with tinned tomatoes and spices. A versatile vegan base that works as a side dish or as a starting point for a more substantial curry.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian home cooking. Tomato and onion masala is the backbone of most British curry-house and home-cooked Indian dishes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in batches as a curry base. Defrost and add protein or vegetables on the day of cooking.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch and freeze in portions to use as a quick base for other curries.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 3 days ahead and store in the fridge. The flavour deepens with time.

content.text: This simple tomato and onion curry is a foundational Anglo-Indian dish. It gives a rich, spiced sauce that works as a side dish on its own or as the base for a bigger curry. Take your time with the onions or the final sauce will taste raw.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and mustard seeds if using. Let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook for 12 minutes until deep golden brown. Stir frequently. This step sets the flavour of the whole dish.
Stir in the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add the fresh tomatoes and salt. Cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down into the onion.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes. Simmer uncovered for 12 minutes until the oil begins to separate at the edges of the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala. Taste and adjust salt. Top with fresh coriander if using.

items.symptom: The curry tastes sweet and raw.
items.cause: The onions were not cooked long enough.
items.fix: Keep cooking the onion over a medium heat until it is a deep golden brown before adding anything else.

items.cause: The tomatoes were not cooked down enough to lose their sharpness.
items.fix: Simmer for a further 5 to 10 minutes uncovered. A pinch of sugar can also balance the acidity.

items.symptom: The sauce is burning at the bottom of the pan.
items.cause: The heat is too high or the sauce has reduced too far.
items.fix: Add a splash of water, reduce the heat, and stir to lift any stuck bits from the base.
